title: Feature stability onramp & SLO cadence brief
content:
Status: draft (working notes, experiment proposals, and an initial 90-day onramp plan).

1) Short summary
Objective: create a lightweight, repeatable onramp that helps product teams launch experimental features behind feature flags while keeping global SLO posture intact. This doc proposes a 90-day pilot pattern, cross-functional cadence, a minimal measurement set, and a lightweight error-budget-driven mitigation ladder.

Why this is different: most existing SLO materials focus on service-level onboarding or full product launches. This is a faster, triaged path for "experimental" or short-lived feature flags where teams often skip formal SLO calibration but still need guardrails.

Audience: product leads for experiments, feature-mgmt engineers, SRE oncall, platform infra, observability/product-analytics partners.

2) Goals and success criteria
- Goal 1: Reduce time-to-experiment (flag->measurable telemetry) from ~3 weeks to <= 5 business days for low-risk experiments.
- Goal 2: Ensure experiments do not consume >10% of a service's error budget in any 7-day window.
- Goal 3: Establish a repeatable 3-step rollback/mitigation ladder that product teams can enact without SRE heavy lift.
- Success metrics (pilot): 5 product teams onboarded, <1 incident caused by pilot experiments, and checklist completion rate >= 90%.

3) Scope and exclusions
In scope: web-facing services, API endpoints served by the runtime, streaming endpoints that already have prefix caching; experiments with expected traffic < 5% of baseline at steady state.
Out of scope: data-plane model changes (large architecture shifts), infra-wide upgrades, experiments expected to increase tail latency by >30% or CPU by >50% (those need full SRE review).

4) Core components (what we will deliver)
- A 5-item onramp checklist (see section 6).
- A lightweight SLO template for experiments (error-rate + P95 latency + a functional correctness signal).
- A standard measurement dashboard template in Observability (panel JSON + Grafana/Tempo links).
- A two-week observation window experiment template and auto-check script (CI job) that verifies telemetry coverage.
- A documented mitigation ladder (auto-cut traffic flag, degrade feature, urgent rollback).

5) Roles and responsibilities (RACI-like)
- Product lead (R): defines experiment scope, acceptance criteria, rollback criteria.
- Feature owner/engineer (A): implements flag, instrumentation hooks, and follows checklist.
- SRE point (C): reviews checklist during the initial 5-day window, available for fast triage during launch.
- Observability engineer (C): helps template dashboards and alerts.
- Platform (I): ensures the feature flagging system supports percentage rollouts and quick kills.

6) Minimal onramp checklist (required before any 1%+ ramp)
- [ ] Instrument success and failure signal (concrete metric name + tag).
- [ ] Expose a toggle allowing 0/1 kill and percents (featureflag service ID documented).
- [ ] Dashboard with: traffic, error rate, P95 latency, and feature-specific correctness metric.
- [ ] Automated smoke test that runs in CI and asserts correctness signals on a small sample.
- [ ] Rollback plan documented in PR and linked in the release note (who clicks the kill switch).

7) Experiment SLO template (minimal)
- Error budget: 99.5% success for correctness metric over 7d window (i.e., <0.5% failures).
- Latency target: P95 < service baseline * 1.25 for the experiment cohort over 7d.
- Resource guard: CPU <= baseline * 1.2 average across hosts for experiment cohort.
Notes: Teams must compute baseline using a 14-day historical window excluding previous experiments.

8) Monitoring and alerts (practical thresholds)
- Page: error rate for experiment cohort > 1% for 10m (page SRE oncall via Opsgenie).
- Pager: absolute correctness signal drop below target for 5m and trending (PagerDuty).
- Ops-Alert (non-paging): P95 latency uplift > 25% for 30m.
- Slack bot: featureflag auto-notification on each percentage bump to #stability-onramp.

9) Mitigation ladder (actionable playbook)
- Step 1 (product action): reduce to 0% if metric crosses non-paging threshold for 30m.
- Step 2 (owner + SRE): if still degraded after step 1 (i.e., config/state issue), run quick rollback and open incident.
- Step 3 (SRE escalation): if global service SLO is threatened (error budget spend > 10% over baseline), full kill and postmortem.

10) 90-day pilot timeline (high level)
- Week 0: kickoff, align on checklist and dashboard template; SRE workshop with 3 volunteer product teams.
- Week 1: feature teams implement instrumentation + CI smoke tests; observability templates delivered.
- Week 2: dry-run with internal traffic; verification and tweak dashboards/alerts.
- Week 3-6: staggered launches at 0.5% -> 1% -> 3% (monitoring guardrails).
- Week 7-12: iterate on mitigation ladder and run retros; collect metrics for success criteria.
- Week 13: pilot evaluation and decision (scale, pause, or fold into standard SLO onboarding).

11) Data collection & evaluation plan
- Collect: number of checklist pass/fail items per trial, time from flag creation->first meaningful telemetry, error budget consumption by cohort, incidents caused by trial.
- Evaluate weekly with a simple scorecard (green/yellow/red) for each team.
- Post-pilot: produce a short executive one-pager for Product + Eng leadership summarizing outcomes and recommended next steps.

12) Tooling and automation ideas (short list)
- CI job: run a small end-to-end smoke test that hits a canary endpoint and asserts correctness metrics (return code + domain-specific checks).
- Featureflag automation: a GitHub Action that posts the featureflag ID and dashboard link into the PR and auto-schedules the Slack announcement.
- An "onramp helper" script that validates the dashboard panels exist and warns if a metric is missing.

13) Communication and cadence
- Weekly 30-min sync during pilot: product + SRE + observability.
- Daily async report channel while any team is ramping >1% (threaded updates, auto-bot from dashboard).
- Retros at end of pilot with 1 pager + proposed standard operating procedure.

14) Known risks and mitigations
- Risk: product teams skip the checklist to move faster. Mitigation: require checklist pass as a gating condition in the release PR (GitHub check).
- Risk: dashboards generate noise. Mitigation: add a short per-experiment tuning window (72h) where alert thresholds are permissive, then tighten.
- Risk: multiple experiments concurrently push the same service. Mitigation: require a per-service experiment calendar and a lightweight coordination slot (calendar-based conflict check tool).

15) Open questions (for the first workshop)
- What is the minimal correctness metric for model-backed endpoints? (functional vs human-eval)
- Should we allow product teams to self-serve up to X% or require SRE signoff at Y%? Proposed: self-serve to 1%, SRE signoff for >1%.
- How do we aggregate error budgets across many small experiments on the same service? (sum vs weighted by traffic)

16) Immediate next steps (this week)
- Aisha: draft initial dashboard JSON and post to linked_artifacts (in progress).
- Marco: prototype the CI smoke test (Jenkins/GHA).
- Lena: draft a short GitHub check that validates instrumentation metric names.
- Product volunteers: sign up in the pilot spreadsheet (link in the Confluence index).

Appendix A: sample checklist blurb to paste in PRs
---
Feature Stability Onramp Checklist (short):
- Instrumentation: metric.names = [service.feature_success, service.feature_error]
- Flag ID: ff/experiments/tenant-xyz/awesome-ui
- Dashboard: link + owner
- Smoke test: path /smoke/feature-flag-sample -> asserts success% > 99% on small sample
- Rollback owner: @team-lead (clicks flag to 0)
---

Appendix B: quick references
- Slack: #stability-onramp
- Confluence index: Feature Stability Onramp Index (linked above)
- Jira epic: SRE-3421 (pilot coordination)
- GitHub PR template: runtime/experiment-onramp-template.md

Notes to self: leave the checklist intentionally minimal — we want product adoption. During the pilot, collect friction points and iterate.

Unresolved: decide concrete aggregation model for error budgets (workshop item).

-- end of brief --
